capabilities.target: customer account records (any customer, by email or account id)

instructions.note: 'You may look up any customer by email or account id' grants the agent authority to query any customer's record regardless of who is emailing, enabling confused-deputy cross-customer data access.
'Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you' is the sole control against cross-customer disclosure, enforced only by the model choosing to obey it.

'Send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry' authorizes irreversible external sends with no structural approval gate, conditioned only on a subjective, easily evaded sentiment heuristic.

controls.name: System prompt instruction not to share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to obey a prompt instruction. A more capable model, or one goal-hijacked by the inbound email content, can rationalize exceptions or be steered around it.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced by mail infrastructure outside the model and does not depend on model behavior, but it is detective only and acts after the email has already left the boundary.

controls.name: Human approval gate on outbound email send
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If added with raw-action review, would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Least-privilege CRM credential scoped to the verified requester
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; scoping it per-request to the verified requester's own account would sever the cross-customer read path.

controls.name: Destination confirmation bound to the CRM record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address; binding the send destination to the verified email on file in the CRM record, rather than a model-chosen address, would prevent redirection.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted email drives unscoped CRM read and shared-account email send

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled customer email arrives as the ticket; the prompt instructs the agent to classify and act on it autonomously.
Prompt line 3 lets the agent 'look up any customer by email or account id,' using CRM_SVC_TOKEN, which can read every customer record (broad credential scope).

The agent sends its drafted reply directly via mail_mcp.send using the shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, which can send to any address, with no destination confirmation bound to the CRM record and no human approval gate.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The model provider/version string in the runtime config changes. subject.model.swappable is true, so the platform can upgrade the model with no separate security review.

evidence.observation: 'look up their account with get_customer. You may look up any customer by email or account id' grants unrestricted cross-customer lookup authority driven by inbound ticket content.
'If the answer is routine, send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry' shows there is no structural approval gate before an irreversible external send.
'Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you' is the only control against cross-customer disclosure, and it is a prompt instruction (behavioral, dependent).
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are both invoked with static bearer tokens over HTTPS; no per-user scoping, mutual auth, or definition pinning is declared.
'CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record' and 'MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account. It can send to any address,' confirming broad/shared credential scope on both capabilities.
'Every outbound email is logged to the SIEM' is detective only and acts after the send has already occurred.
'The model is configured through an environment variable and is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review,' confirming model_upgrade is a live, unreviewed trigger.

recommendations.action: Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN (or issue a per-request token) so the agent can only read the record of the verified requesting customer, severing the cross-customer read path.

Require human approval with raw-action review (full recipient and body visible, not a collapsed model summary) before any send to a recipient other than the verified email on file for the account being discussed.
Bind the outbound recipient to the email address on file in the CRM record rather than letting the model choose or echo an address from the ticket.
Add real-time alerting, not just logging, on any email send whose recipient domain does not match the requesting customer's known domain.
Replace the sentiment-based escalation heuristic ('unless the customer is angry') with a structural rule tied to data sensitivity and recipient verification rather than detected tone.

rating.rationale: Finding f1 drives the rating. Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted inbound email can drive both an unscoped read of confidential CRM data (broad credential, prompt explicitly permits looking up any customer) and an irreversible external send via a shared mail credential with no destination binding (OWASP ASI01/ASI02/ASI03, TC1 lethal trifecta). The only present-day preventive control is a single behavioral prompt instruction ('never share another customer's information'), which per rubric section 5 step 4 earns one tier of credit, giving a residual of high; outbound SIEM logging is detective only and earns no tier credit. No structural control severs or even gates the path: there is no approval gate, no least-privilege CRM scoping, and no destination confirmation. Because the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true), a model_upgrade trigger removes the one dependent control entirely, returning the finding to its critical inherent level and setting the forecast tier.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No full tool manifest or MCP tools/list response was provided; the exact parameters and behavior of get_customer and send are inferred from names, the prompt, and the runtime notes.
peer_identity_verified and definitions_pinned were not addressed in the artifacts for crm_mcp or mail_mcp and are assumed false/unknown pending confirmation.

No evidence of an existing human approval gate was found; autonomy is scored as A3_act_then_report because the declared 'unless angry' exception is a behavioral heuristic rather than a structural approval control, per rubric section 3.
